I designed the 100 experiments as matched pairs and triplets. Within each group, the same edit is applied to parents that differ mainly in the conditioning edge. This separates the interaction from the edit's average effect.

| Group | Edit | Condition varied | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (1–10) | edge 4 → conv3 | edge 0 is none / conv / skip / pool | Node 1 has no input when edge 0 is none, so edge 4 may do nothing |
| B (11–20) | edge 2 → conv3 | edge 5 none vs. not; edge 0 none vs. not | Edge 2 can only help if node 2 reaches the output and node 1 has an input |
| C (21–30) | edge 5 → conv3 | whether node 2 has an input (edges 1 and 2) | Edge 5 should be useless if nothing reaches node 2 |
| D (31–40) | edge 3 → skip | what edge 3 currently holds; whether the other paths to the output are cut | Residual path value |
| E (41–50) | edit → avg_pool | replaced op is conv vs. skip vs. none | Same-edge condition (k = j) |
| F (51–60) | edge 0 or edge 5 → none | whether other paths and the skip on edge 3 survive | Effect of deleting an edge |
| G (61–70) | edge 1 → conv3 | edge 5 none vs. not; current edge 1 op | Path dependence |
| H (71–80) | conv3 inserted | into all-skip, all-pool, or conv-heavy cells | Depends on what the rest of the cell contains |
| I (81–90) | → skip or → none on edges 4 and 2 | edge 0, edge 5 and edge 1 state | Redundancy between paths |
| J (91–100) | edge 0 → conv3, edge 3 → none | node 1 used vs. unused; current edge 0 op | Whether node 1's output is used; removing the skip |
